alternatives: he borrowed | the book | He | promised | to return
BAS3-05.note: Swap the two clauses: 'He borrowed the book he promised to return.' The 'he borrowed' chip opens the sentence and the 'He' chip becomes the subject of the relative clause. Fully grammatical and natural; the meaning changes but the grammar holds.

BAS3-08.note: Marginal: the question 'is it important to read the instructions carefully' works only if a question mark is allowed, and no punctuation may be added.

BAS3-09.note: Marginal: the question 'is she afraid of losing her job' needs a question mark.

BAS3-10.note: Marginal: the question 'are we looking forward to seeing you' needs a question mark and reads oddly.

BAS3-17.note: 'The old car expected nobody to start so easily' is grammatical but makes no sense. Not natural.

alternatives: Everyone | enjoyed | the concert | except | my brother
BAS3-21.note: Moving the except-phrase to the end gives 'Everyone enjoyed the concert except my brother.' This is fully natural, arguably more common than the key.

BAS3-23.note: 'I didn't realize how late was it' is ungrammatical because an embedded question keeps normal word order.

BAS3-24.note: Marginal topicalization: 'Why I had left, he wanted to know' needs a comma and reads as literary.

BAS3-25.note: Marginal: the question 'is this the first time I have flown alone' needs a question mark.

BAS3-27.note: Marginal: the question 'is the old museum well worth a visit' needs a question mark.

BAS3-29.note: Marginal: the question 'had we run out of printer paper' needs a question mark.

BAS3-30.note: Marginal: the question 'were the children far too excited to sleep' needs a question mark.

BAS3-33.note: Marginal: the question 'is there no point in arguing' needs a question mark.

alternatives: she had trained for | the race | She | managed | to finish
BAS3-34.note: The same clause swap as BAS3-05 gives 'She had trained for the race she managed to finish.' Grammatical and natural.

BAS3-35.note: Marginal: 'In English, our teacher strongly recommends reading the novel' (fronting, needs a comma). 'Recommends reading in English the novel' is unnatural.

BAS3-37.note: Marginal: the question 'was it kind of you to help' needs a question mark.

BAS3-39.note: Marginal: the question 'is he likely to arrive late' needs a question mark.

BAS3-42.note: Marginal: the question 'was she the only one who noticed' needs a question mark.

BAS3-43.note: Marginal: the question 'were the students asked to hand in their essays' needs a question mark.

BAS3-48.note: Marginal: the question 'is it no use complaining about it' needs a question mark and is awkward.
